seasons.title: Blood Nourishment
seasons.arc_summary: The party starts as rookie couriers in Hallia and stumbles into a sprawling conspiracy — Ugathul monsters posing as Blackline cops, Embercall radar dishes spreading a destructive resonance, and Grayson's necromantic experiments beneath the city. After a catastrophic near-total party kill at the Crowded Flea, the survivors are resurrected through the Black and White, regroup, and slay both Hlarf and Tywelwyn Leatherhide — uncovering the existence of six Thessian gods attempting to crack the Firmament.

seasons.title: The Pilgrimage
seasons.arc_summary: In the aftermath of Tywelwyn's death, the party reports their findings to the Inquisition, rescues Anaïs from an Aut-branded trap (learning of the Narrative — five cosmic siblings), and enters the Pilgrimage scavenger hunt at Ragged Roost. Through puzzle-solving, art theft, diplomacy with the Heart Rapid Connection, and a bloody ambush by Concordia, they secure Keystone 14 and passage aboard the colossal Strider.

seasons.title: The Firmament Fracture
seasons.arc_summary: Argyle returns in half-form as the party enters extended downtime, then descends into Hallia's sewers toward quarantined Teller's Run. They discover a crack in the Firmament imprisoning a two-mile-tall figure, hack a terminal exposing Grayson's and the Prime Minister's conspiracy to shatter reality, bomb the research facility, and flee through a collapsing underground — triggering a mushroom cloud of ash over Teller's Run as the Harlequin announces the Strider's imminent departure.

seasons.title: The Strider
seasons.arc_summary: The party boards the colossal Strider and settles into a new world of faction politics, heart-based base-building, and the Harlequin's deadly Tithe. After surviving a void portal eruption on the gala dance floor, harvesting rival hearts for energy, and forging a coalition of allied factions, they descend into the Undercroft and ally with the ancient Machine God — clearing the Strider's depths of Herald cultists and claiming its infrastructure for the Coalition.

seasons.title: The Ashen Pact
seasons.arc_summary: The Coalition consolidates power through loyalty oaths and the Void Atlas, but escalating threats converge: the sleeping clan's hospital is cleared at terrible cost, Anzu discovers the Ashen Pact — six entities overseeing reality — and in a desperate bid for cosmic allies, the party contacts the Menhir and receives a god-killing revolver. When Argyle shoots a Menhir to escape, the entire Narrative turns hostile, the Strider is flung far starward to a dead scoured world, and the Harlequins are annihilated — leaving the party stranded off every known map.

seasons.title: Far Starward
seasons.arc_summary: Stranded on a godless horizon, the party rallies the surviving factions, rescues a half-minotaur gunslinger from the Herald's song, infiltrates the Strider's corrupted spire, and pursues Anzu's sister Galzu through three surreal vignettes of history into Tali's Fane. A far-range expedition to the wrecked Hesperid yields phlogiston fuel and first contact with castaway Sedecium researchers, who reveal the Ashen Pact's newly ascended members — culminating in the party diving into Esoterica's lair and destroying the nascent god with the god-killing gun.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.arc_summary: Three Actinium Convox operatives — Banyan, Giancarlo Santucci, and Crindle Vilksnake — are tasked with deploying the "Midnight Sun" bomb in a Raelion Fane atop a ley line. They infiltrate the city of Orilon via river and sewer, find the bone-tree heart of the Fane, and in a desperate combat activate the monolith just before its countdown completes — obliterating all of Raelion. The session is set 20 years before the main campaign.

seasons.title: The Heist and the Forge
seasons.arc_summary: The party kidnaps Yudan from the Leviathan, forges an uneasy alliance, and ventures into Oresk's underground ruins. After rescuing the mercenary Damien and awakening a nascent divine forge, they plead their case before the Narrative to obtain a godpiercer needle of Holy Gold.

seasons.title: The Hunted and the Heist
seasons.arc_summary: Exposed by Insuperlex's planet-wide broadcast, the party flees Oresk through the tundra to Sarengrad, allies with the Golden Sparrows, and infiltrates the First House's RC3 research facility floor by floor. After killing Rampart and ambushing Karkov, they steal the Divinity Leech and escape — only for the Broker to whisk them to an entirely new world.

seasons.title: Syrin and the Golden Spire
seasons.arc_summary: Arriving on the cyberpunk planet Syrin, the party crashes MediaCon to trace the Feep's trail to Omnivox's orbital headquarters. After surviving a space-shard disaster and ascending the Gilded Spire, they confront and slay the god-wannabe Immix in a climactic multi-phase battle.

seasons.title: Vesper Feep Must Die
seasons.arc_summary: Empowered by Immix's divine energy, the party learns the Feep's true name and origin — Vesper Feep, a street orphan turned media mogul — and grows backup clones before their final assault. They pin him to the weave with the godpiercer needle and kill him, but his death tears open the Slip and sets the stage for the Deep.

seasons.title: The Deep and the Lighthouse
seasons.arc_summary: The party ascends to the 13th Realm and descends into the City in Yellow, completing six shaping trials before battling the Deep as the moon crashes into Althane. Victorious, the Lighthouse quarantines the world and carries the Weft onward; the newly demigod party then convenes the First Council of Althane to reshape the future.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.arc_summary: A Die Hard–style holiday one-shot set in Calaria's capital, Halnia. Hildebrandt Corporation employees Atsuki, Mika Buzzle, Vint, and Chris Gangle attend a Bright Souls Eve party at headquarters, only for a terrorist named Naren Rodder to seize the building. After clearing the ballroom of captors and discovering Director of Strategy Vitor Frey is a traitor, the team climbs to the vault floor and engages Naren—who is blessed by the Heir of the Plague—in a desperate fight that ends with the Plague Codex launched out a blown-out wall into the unknown.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.arc_summary: In the first session of a new Færrin-set one-shot (now a two-shot), four members of the Velvet Mark — Archie, Salvatore, Branson, and Combo — are tasked by Father Marone to assassinate the Spark, leader of the upstart gang Pyrelight. En route to Teller's Run, they're pulled over by Threshold Authority officers, leading to a violent car chase that ends with the cops' car flipped and destroyed. After ditching their identifiable car at Feathers' shop for a disguise, they sneak into Teller's Run and discover the Spark presiding over a burning-stage spectacle with a cheering crowd.

shows.name: A Hunt of Metal and Vine

seasons.title: The Joker World Expedition
seasons.arc_summary: The show opens by wrapping up a Cagley Middle School one-shot against the Terror of Cagley, then pivots to a new Scale campaign: four high-ranking operatives investigate a slip-shielded structure on a shattered Joker World, battling through demon hordes, solving the fiendish puzzle-tower called the Quorum, and ultimately rescuing Voice of Many — a trapped divine entity and grandchild of the Judge — before teleporting back to Scale headquarters.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.arc_summary: In a one-shot set months before the main campaign, three Undercroft workers — Barlow Crane, Grant FireEye, and Gage the Cunning — investigate sabotage aboard the massive moving Strider city of Iomenei. Tracking an elven suspect named Gerhardt into a long-abandoned forsaken sector, they discover an insectoid infestation centered on a dormant engine heart cathedral and must slay a massive Swarm Hive Mother. Though they halt the infestation, the true saboteur remains at large.

seasons.title: The Everdawn Drift
seasons.arc_summary: Three Sedecium agents investigate an unpowered orbital station partially sunk into the slip, uncovering that the Thessian Esoterica tortured the station's AI and accessed records of a massive magical spike near the Astra's core.

seasons.title: One Last Job
seasons.arc_summary: Pulled from retirement, the fire team boards a Sundom planet-killer warship to steal divine essence from the freshly-killed Thessian god Tithe before the God Eater Harrow finishes devouring it — navigating slip puzzles and spider temples to become the only team to succeed.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.arc_summary: A D&D 5e one-shot set on the Finnegan Ring caravan route. Three caravan members — Mango the elven ranger, Doug Donahue the gnome rogue, and Egan the orc druid — are transported along with flautist Erin Proudcloak to a fey swampland by a mysterious mist. There, the fey creature Larunan forces them to fight for his amusement in an arena battle full of chaotic magical effects. The party survives and is returned to the caravan.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.arc_summary: When a goblin intern at Bisney & Dixar Animated Studios connects a new arcane intelligence to the studio's databases, the AI overloads and casts a spell that engulfs Los Diablos in a blackout and creates a 'movie' on the island of Afro-China. Three Disney villains — Hades, Fulton (Gaston's legally distinct cousin), and Runway Brian (a forgotten Disney short mouse) — are chosen by a mandrill statue of Zeus to recover an enchanted mirror stolen by Maui, now hidden in an Elephant Graveyard of Wonders. After surviving a wildebeest stampede, solving the Cave of Wonders' riddle, defeating the hybrid genie Jaskar (Jafar-Scar fusion), and wishing themselves past a whole skipped sequence to the final soundstage, the trio battles the Legally Distinct Nostalgia Hydra — a five-headed amalgamation of iconic Disney characters that undergoes a terrifying live-action reboot mid-fight. They slay it, seize the mirror, and dive through it into the real world.
